scene: Petitions of the dead; Virgil and Sordello recognize a shared homeland; Dante laments divided Italy
story: A crowd of souls presses around Dante, each asking him to remember them among the living. Virgil guides Dante onward while allowing their appeals to be heard.

Dante asks how prayers can help those awaiting ascent, recalling Virgil's earlier words about the apparent immutability of divine judgment. Virgil distinguishes the situations and tells him Beatrice will illuminate the matter further.
The travelers find a solitary soul looking on with dignity. Virgil asks for directions, and the soul first asks their country of origin.
When Virgil names Mantua, the soul reveals himself as Sordello, also Mantuan. The two embrace immediately, united by their shared home.
Dante contrasts the warmth between these two compatriots with the conflict among Italian cities. His poem turns to an extended lament over faction, poor leadership and the suffering of Italy.
The embrace does not erase civic division; it exposes how different the world could be. The travelers remain on the mountain, with Sordello to guide them in the next canto.

semanticSomatic.semantic: Many requests can reach one witness without becoming one undifferentiated claim

Individual solidarity can reveal a contrast with collective division
